These exercises practise the graphs from Chapter 4. The first run takes a little longer while your browser downloads ggplot2. Where you see `______`, replace it with your own code.

```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: [ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4, ex5, ex6]
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
students  <- read.csv("students.csv")
semesters <- read.csv("semesters.csv")
first_sem <- semesters |>
  filter(semester == 1) |>
  left_join(students, join_by(student_id))
```

## The basic graphs

### Exercise 1: A histogram

Draw a histogram of `study_hours` in the first semester. Try binwidths of 1, 5, and 10. Which shows the shape best?

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex1
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = ______)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5)
```

::: { .solution exercise="ex1" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = study_hours)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5)
```

A binwidth of 1 hour is noisy, 10 hours hides the shape, and about 5 hours shows it best: most students study between about 10 and 45 hours a week, and only a few study 55 hours or more.
:::
:::

### Exercise 2: A bar chart in one colour

Draw a bar chart of how many students have each level of `employment`, with all bars in a colour of your choice. Should the colour go inside or outside `aes()`?

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex2
ggplot(students, aes(x = employment)) +
  geom_bar(______)
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex2" }
::: { .callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

A fixed colour is *set*, outside `aes()`: `geom_bar(fill = "darkorange")`.
:::
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex2" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
ggplot(students, aes(x = employment)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "darkorange")
```
:::
:::

### Exercise 3: Box plots with labels

Draw box plots of first-semester GPA for each faculty, with the axis labels "Faculty" and "GPA (0 to 4)".

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex3
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = faculty, y = gpa)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = ______, y = ______)
```

::: { .solution exercise="ex3" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = faculty, y = gpa)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Faculty", y = "GPA (0 to 4)")
```
:::
:::

### Exercise 4: A scatter plot with a trend line

Draw caffeine against sleep in the first semester, with partly transparent points and a straight trend line. What does it suggest?

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex4
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = caffeine_mg, y = sleep_hours)) +
  geom_point(alpha = ______) +
  geom_smooth(method = ______)
```

::: { .solution exercise="ex4" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = caffeine_mg, y = sleep_hours)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```

Students who take more caffeine sleep less. Chapter 7 shows why this matters when you study caffeine and grades.
:::
:::

## Making graphs ready to share

### Exercise 5: Mapping colour

Draw a density plot of first-semester wellbeing with one curve per `study_mode`. This time the colour depends on the data, so where does `fill` go? Add `alpha = 0.5` so both curves are visible.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex5
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = wellbeing, ______)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5)
```

::: { .solution exercise="ex5" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = wellbeing, fill = study_mode)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5)
```

Colour that depends on a variable is *mapped*, inside `aes()`.
:::
:::

### Exercise 6: Facets and a theme

Redo your scatter plot from Exercise 4 with one panel per `programme`, clear labels, and `theme_minimal()`.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex6
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = caffeine_mg, y = sleep_hours)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ ______) +
  labs(x = "Caffeine per day (mg)", y = "Sleep per night (hours)") +
  ______()
```

::: { .solution exercise="ex6" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
ggplot(first_sem, aes(x = caffeine_mg, y = sleep_hours)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ programme) +
  labs(x = "Caffeine per day (mg)", y = "Sleep per night (hours)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
:::
:::
